@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+---
+authors: Liying Jiang
+state: final
+---
+
+# RFD0: JobWorker Service Design 
+
+## What
+Need to implement a jobWorker service that can run arbitrary Linux processes. Also need to provide a CLI tool to interract with the jobWorker service.
+
+## Why
+For demonstration.
+
+## Details
+
+### Requirements
+* The jobWorker service should be able to provide below APIs:
+  * Start a linux process which is called `job`
+  * Stop a running job
+  * Get status of a job
+  * Stream output of a job, and output should be from start of process execution.
+
+* The service needs to support multiple concurrent clients and requests
+   
+* The service needs to have resource control for CPU, Memory and Disk IO per job using cgroups
+
+
+* The job service need to have auth: 
+  * Use mTLS authentication and verify client certificate. 
+  * Use a simple authorization scheme.
+
+
+Also need to create a CLI tool:
+* User can use the CLI to connect to the jobWorker service and start, stop, get status, and stream output of a job.
+
+
+### Detailed Design
+#### Implement the jobWorker service using gRPC.
+ The gRPC server is multithreaded and can simultaneously accept connections from multiple clients.
+
+   The  Protocol Buffers (protobuf) file is like below:
+   ```
+   syntax = "proto3";
+
+   package worker;
+
+
+   service JobWorker {
+      rpc StartJob(JobRequest) returns (JobResponse) {}
+      rpc StopJob(JobID) returns () {}
+      rpc GetJobStatus(JobID) returns (JobStatusResponse) {}
+      rpc StreamJobOutput(JobID) returns (stream JobOutput) {}
+   }
+
+   message JobRequest {
+      string command = 1;
+      int64 cpu_limit = 2;
+      int64 mem_limit = 3;
+      int64 io_limit = 4;
+   }
+
+   message JobResponse {
+      int64 job_id = 1;
+   }
+
+   message JobID {
+      int64 job_id = 1;
+   }
+
+   message JobStatusResponse {
+      enum Status {
+         PENDING = 0;
+         RUNNING = 1;
+         COMPLETED = 2;
+         FAILED = 3;
+         STOPPED = 4;
+      }
+
+      int64 job_id = 1;
+      Status status = 2;
+      int64 duration = 3; 
+      string start_time = 4;
+   }
+
+   message JobOutput {
+      string output = 1;
+   }
+   ```
+
+   As the jobWorker service needs to execute multiple linux commands(process), and some commands can take long time to execute; to avoid blocking the server, we will start `go routine` for each command. Inside the go routine, it will start the execution of the command and read the output and save it to a memory block, then return. 
+
+   We will have a global job map that stores all the jobs and theire metadata and job output in memory. The issue is that when the server runs for a long time or some jobs have large outputs, the server will consume big amount of memories. For this project, for simplicity, we assume there are unlimited memories/resources the server can use. So we will not do many optimizations on this. For futhure improvements, for example, we can consider to offload the old jobs or job's output has been read or low priority job etc. into file system or other external storage to save memeory. Also can consider to clear out job output from the memory once it has been read if this is ok with the user requirements.     
+
+   For `cgroup`, my current dev box is a Macbook, so I may not be able to test the code. I may add the creation of `cgroup` code in the implementation, but may not be able to test it out.
+
+#### Implement mTLS
+  
+  For this project, we will generate self-signed certificate using openssl as root certificate. We will generate cerficates and keys individually for jobWorker service and CLI client, and signed them with the root cert. When doing connection, both server and client will provide certificate and verify.
+  
+  For simplicity, we will hard-coded the path on where to load certificate files. 
+  
+  For future improvement, it is good to set configuration file and specify the path of certificates. 
+
+#### Authorization
+  Authorization mechanisms control access to resources based on the identity of the requester and the permissions they have. Typical authorization mechanism includes:
+  * Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
+  * Policy-Based Access Control
+  * Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)
+  * Access Control Lists (ACLs)
+  * Context-Based Access Control
+  
+  For simplicity, I will implement a simple ACLs 
+
+#### CLI tool
+  
+  There are multiple command-line parsing libraries. For this projects, we don't have specific requirements and most libraries should work. I will use github.com/urfave/cli as I have used it before.
+  
+  The commands will look like below:
+  ```
+    
+   To start a job
+   % ./client-cli start -command ls
+   Job ID: 1
+
+
+   To get job status
+   % ./client-cli get -id 1   
+   Job status: COMPLETED
+   Job startTime: 2024-04-26 02:17:49
+   Job duration: 6508520
+
+   To stop a job 
+   % ./client-cli stop -id 1   
+
+   To get job ouput
+   % ./client-cli output -id 1   
+   main.go
+   server.go
+   ...
+
+```
+
+### Security
+
+This project uses certificate for auth, may need to consider certificate expiration cycle, and store certificate in a safe place etc.
+
+### Privacy
+
+
+### UX
+
+Implement a client CLI tool
+
+
+### Proto Specification
+
+N/A
+### Backward Compatibility
+
+N/A
+### Audit Events
+
+N/A
+
+### Observability
+
+N/A
+### Product Usage
+
+N/A
+
+### Test Plan
+
+We will write go unit tests for major APIs.
+
+Tests should cover:
+* StartJob()
+* StopJob()
+* GetJobStatus()
+* GetJobOutput()
+* mTLS with valid cert
+* mTLS with invalid cert
+* User with unauthorized actions
+* JobWorker service can process multiple requests simultaneously (optional)
+

@@ -0,0 +1,244 @@
+---
+authors: Liying Jiang
+state: final
+---
+
+# RFD0: JobWorker Service Design 
+
+## What
+Need to implement a jobWorker service that can run arbitrary Linux processes. Also need to provide a CLI tool to interract with the jobWorker service.
+
+## Why
+For demonstration.
+
+## Details
+
+### Requirements
+* The jobWorker service should be able to provide below APIs:
+  * Start a linux process which is called `job`
+  * Stop a running job
+  * Get status of a job
+  * Stream output of a job, and output should be from start of process execution.
+
+* The service needs to support multiple concurrent clients and requests
+   
+* The service needs to have resource control for CPU, Memory and Disk IO per job using cgroups
+
+
+* The job service need to have auth: 
+  * Use mTLS authentication and verify client certificate. 
+  * Use a simple authorization scheme.
+
+
+Also need to create a CLI tool:
+* User can use the CLI to connect to the jobWorker service and start, stop, get status, and stream output of a job.
+
+
+### Detailed Design
+#### Implement the jobWorker service using gRPC.
+ The gRPC server is multithreaded and can simultaneously accept connections from multiple clients.
+
+   The  Protocol Buffers (protobuf) file is like below:
+   ```
+   syntax = "proto3";
+
+   package worker;
+
+   import "google/protobuf/timestamp.proto";
+
+   service JobWorker {
+      rpc StartJob(JobRequest) returns (JobResponse) {}
+      rpc StopJob(JobID) returns (Empty) {}
+      rpc GetJobStatus(JobID) returns (JobStatusResponse) {}
+      rpc StreamJobOutput(JobID) returns (stream JobOutput) {}
+   }
+
+   message JobRequest {
+      string command = 1;
+   }
+
+   message JobResponse {
+      int64 job_id = 1;
+   }
+
+   message JobID {
+      int64 job_id = 1;
+   }
+
+   message JobStatusResponse {
+      enum Status {
+         PENDING = 0;
+         RUNNING = 1;
+         COMPLETED = 2;
+         FAILED = 3;
+         STOPPED = 4;
+      }
+
+      int64 job_id = 1;
+      Status status = 2;
+      int64 duration = 3; 
+      google.protobuf.Timestamp start_time = 4;
+   }
+
+   message JobOutput {
+      bytes output = 1;
+   }
+
+   message Empty {}
+   ```
+
+   As the jobWorker service needs to execute multiple linux commands(process), and some commands can take long time to execute; to avoid blocking the server, we will start `go routine` for each command. Inside the go routine, it will start the execution of the command and read the output as byte array and save it to a memory block, then return. 
+
+   We will have a global jobs map that stores all the jobs and theire metadata and job output in memory. The structure is:
+   
+```
+jobs map[int64]*Process // Map to store existing jobs
+
+type Process struct {
+	pid       int
+	status    pb.JobStatusResponse_Status
+	startTime time.Time
+	duration  time.Duration
+	output    []byte
+	req       *pb.JobRequest
+}
+```
+
+ And we will have a never end for loop function to keep read the jobs map, if found new job that has not been processed, then start a go routing to process the job. In details:
+
+   - `ProcessAllJobs()`: iterate through JobServer.jobs map; if a job is in `Pending` state, then start a go routing to start the command, and keep reading output from stdpipe and append the result to the process.output the []byte in the job map
+   - `StartJob()`: add the job to the map
+   - `StopJob()`:  execute "kill -9 pid" to stop the job
+   - `GetJob()`: read job map to get current job status
+   - `Output()`: read the jobs[jobid].Process.output and call Send() to send in stream. The stream gRPC api is a non blocking call and can be execute asynchronically, and support up to 100 calls simutaneously
+  
+
+   One issue with the global job map is that when the server runs for a long time or some jobs have large outputs, the server will consume big amount of memories. For this project, for simplicity, we assume there are unlimited memories/resources the server can use. So we will not do many optimizations on this. For futhure improvements, for example, we can consider to offload the old jobs or job's output has been read or low priority job etc. into file system or other external storage to save memeory. Also can consider to clear out job output from the memory once it has been read if this is ok with the user requirements.     
+
+   For `cgroup`,  we will use cgroups v2; will utilize syscall.CgroupConfig library to create a cgroup attributes, and then run command with cgroup attributes to enforce the cgroup settings. The limits for all commands are:
+   
+   ```
+   memLimit := cgroups.NewMemoryResource(30 * 1024 * 1024) // 30 MB memory limit
+    cpuLimit := cgroups.NewCPUResource(1000000)              // 1s CPU time limit
+    ioLimit := cgroups.NewIOResource()                      // I/O limits
+   ioLimit.SetMaxReadBPS(100 * 1024 * 1024) // Set maximum read bytes limit to 100 MB/s
+   ioLimit.SetMaxWriteIOPS(1000) // Set maximum write operations limit to 1000/s
+   ```
+
+
+
+#### Implement mTLS
+  
+  For this project, we will generate self-signed certificate using openssl as root certificate. We will generate cerficates and keys individually for jobWorker service and CLI client, and signed them with the root cert. When doing connection, both server and client will provide certificate and verify.
+  
+  Sample openssl:
+  ```
+  openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout ca.key -x509 -sha256 -days 365 -out ca.crt -nodes
+```
+
+  For simplicity, we will hard-coded the path on where to load certificate files. 
+  
+  For future improvement, it is good to set configuration file and specify the path of certificates. 
+
+#### Authorization
+  Authorization mechanisms control access to resources based on the identity of the requester and the permissions they have. Typical authorization mechanism includes:
+  * Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
+  * Policy-Based Access Control
+  * Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)
+  * Access Control Lists (ACLs)
+  * Context-Based Access Control
+  
+  For simplicity, I will implement a simple ACLs. On server side, we will have a access list file (in JSON format) that specify which email is allowed and what actions are allowed. For each request coming in, read the client certificate and check against the access list. Sample ACL file:
+  ```
+  {
+  "resources": [
+    {
+      "id": 1,
+      "name": "StartJob",
+      "access": [
+        "user1@example.com",
+        "user2@it.com"
+      ]
+    },
+    {
+      "id": 2,
+      "name": "StopJob",
+      "access": [
+        "admin@example.com"
+      ]
+    }
+    {
+      "id": 3,
+      "name": "GetJob",
+      "access": [
+        "*"
+      ]
+    }
+    {
+      "id": 4,
+      "name": "Output",
+      "access": [
+        "user1@example.com",
+        "user2@it.com"
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+
+#### CLI tool
+  
+  There are multiple command-line parsing libraries. For this projects, we don't have specific requirements and most libraries should work. I will use github.com/urfave/cli as I have used it before.
+  
+  The commands will look like below:
+  ```
+    
+   To start a job
+   % ./client-cli start -command ls
+   Job ID: 1
+
+
+   To get job status
+   % ./client-cli get -id 1   
+   Job status: COMPLETED
+   Job startTime: 2024-04-26 02:17:49
+   Job duration: 7ms
+
+   To stop a job 
+   % ./client-cli stop -id 1   
+
+   To get job ouput
+   % ./client-cli output -id 1   
+   main.go
+   server.go
+   ...
+
+```
+
+### Security
+
+This project uses certificate for auth, may need to consider certificate expiration cycle, and store certificate in a safe place etc.
+
+
+
+### UX
+
+Implement a client CLI tool
